div.head: Hl 16.3
div.ab: Gif he þanne þæt ne mæge gecyþan mid rihtre canne, læte þanne án, ⁊ se agend tofó.
Gif he þanne þæt ne mæge gecyþan mid rihtre canne, læte þanne án, ⁊ se agend tofó.
Gif he þanne þæt ne mæge gecyþan mid rihtre canne, læte þanne án, ⁊ se agend tofó.
Wenn er [der Verklagte] aber das nicht mit gesetzlichem Reinigungseide erklären kann, dann lasse er [sie] los und der Eigenthümer [Kläger] greife zu.
But if he [the accused] cannot declare that with a lawful oath of exculpation, then let him let [them] go and let the owner [the plaintiff] take hold of them.
If, however, he cannot prove that by lawful declaration, he shall give it up, and the owner shall take possession of it.
If, then, he cannot declare that with proper exculpation, he is to relinquish it, and the owner is to succeed to it.
If he cannot then declare that by lawful cognizance, let him then relinquish [it], and the owner take possession.

note.seg: Ausser dem Verlust des Angeschlagenen leidet er Busse und Strafe für Diebstahl laut anderer Germanischer, darunter auch Englischer Rechte; s. Gl Anefang 17; Brunner II 508
Besides losing the thing attached, he incurs compensation and penalty for theft according to other Germanic laws, English ones among them; see Gl Anefang 17; Brunner II 508
i.e. that he bought the property openly, etc.
For a detailed account of the procedure involved in vouching to warranty see B. and T. s.v. team (iii.); see also Pollock and Maitland, History of English Law, i. p. 34 f.
